skill.name: defi-protocol-templates
skill.description: Create DeFi smart contract templates for staking, AMMs, governance, and flash loan workflows. Use for Solidity prototyping that still needs tests, review, and audit.
skill.summary: Create Solidity DeFi templates for protocol prototypes that require later testing and audit.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Solidity require statements and Markdown code fences. No prompt injection, host command execution, or system reconnaissance was found. One medium semantic concern remains because the skill markets simplified value-bearing contract examples as production-ready.

remediation.issue: Production-ready wording overstates the safety of financial contract examples.
remediation.suggestion: Describe the snippets as reference templates, and require expert review, tests, and audit before deployment.

remediation.issue: The package references resource and asset files that are not included in the file structure.
remediation.suggestion: Include the referenced files or remove those claims so users know what the skill actually ships.

semantic_findings.title: Overstated Production Readiness For DeFi Contracts
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md labels the snippets as production-ready while presenting simplified contracts that handle tokens and flash loans. This could lead users to over-trust unaudited financial code.

content.value_statement: DeFi teams need clear starting points for common protocol patterns. This skill provides Solidity-oriented templates and review prompts for staking, AMMs, governance, and flash loans.
actual_capabilities: Provides inline Solidity examples for staking rewards, AMM pools, governance voting, and flash loan flows.
Shows core state variables, events, and functions for each included contract pattern.
Uses OpenZeppelin imports in the staking and governance examples.
Lists best practices for testing, audits, monitoring, upgrades, and emergency controls.
Helps frame prompts for adapting templates to a specific token or protocol design.
limitations: The shipped skill contains only SKILL.md, so referenced assets and reference files are not included.
The examples are not audited and should not be deployed without expert review.
Lending protocol content is mentioned but no inline lending contract is included.
The templates omit full test suites, deployment scripts, and threat models.

use_cases.title: Prototype A Staking Product
use_cases.description: Create a staking rewards outline with deposit, withdrawal, reward accounting, and exit flows.

use_cases.title: Plan Liquidity Pool Mechanics
use_cases.description: Use the AMM example to discuss reserves, shares, swap fees, and liquidity removal behavior.

use_cases.title: Review Governance And Flash Loans
use_cases.description: Map voting periods, proposal thresholds, receiver callbacks, fees, and repayment checks before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Staking Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staking rewards outline for an ERC-20 token. Include state, user actions, events, and audit questions.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt The AMM Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the AMM template for two ERC-20 tokens. Explain reserve updates, LP shares, fees, and slippage controls.

prompt_templates.title: Design Governance Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a governance flow using token voting. Include proposal thresholds, voting windows, execution checks, and timelock needs.

prompt_templates.title: Harden A Flash Loan Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the flash loan template for production risks. Identify missing controls, repayment assumptions, and test cases.

output_examples.input: Create a staking rewards plan for an LP token.
output_examples.output: A structured plan covering token inputs, reward accounting, stake and withdraw actions, events, and audit checks.

output_examples.input: Review the AMM example before adapting it.
output_examples.output: A review that explains reserves, share minting, swap pricing, fee assumptions, and missing slippage protections.

output_examples.input: Assess the flash loan flow for safety gaps.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering receiver trust, callback behavior, repayment verification, reentrancy, fee handling, and integration tests.

best_practices: Treat every template as a starting point, not a deployable contract.
Add unit tests, fuzz tests, integration tests, and invariant checks before deployment.
Use independent security review for any contract that can hold user funds.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy the snippets directly to mainnet.
Do not assume referenced resource files exist in the installed package.
Do not add flash loan or AMM logic without slippage, access, and reentrancy review.

faq.question: Can I deploy these contracts as written?
faq.answer: No. Use them as references, then add tests, threat modeling, and professional audit work.

faq.question: Which protocol patterns are included?
faq.answer: The file includes staking, AMM, governance token, governor, flash loan provider, and receiver examples.

faq.question: Does the skill include a lending contract?
faq.answer: No. Lending is mentioned, but the packaged file does not include an inline lending contract.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are tests or deployment scripts included?
faq.answer: No. You must create tests, deployment scripts, and network configuration separately.

faq.question: What should I review first?
faq.answer: Review token transfer safety, reentrancy, access controls, oracle assumptions, slippage checks, and upgrade permissions.
